verdict.rationale: YubiKey's own FIDO2 implementation requires user presence (a physical touch) for cryptographic operations, including FIDO2-backed SSH keys. Any automated action routed through those keys therefore cannot complete without a human touch, and a community comment confirms the touch-to-sign model resists remote abuse. Nothing documents framing or configuring this as an approval gate for agent-initiated or automated actions, so applying it to agent workflows depends on integrating through signing or SSH. missing for 10: documented agent or automation approval workflows, per-action policy for requiring touch on sensitive operations, independent hands-on corroboration of use as an agent approval step.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can require a physical key touch as the human-approval step for sensitive automated or agent-initiated actions

citations.quote: FIDO2 also requires user presence (a touch on your YubiKey) for cryptographic operations, and can optionally enforce user verification (PIN entry).
This guide shows how to generate and use SSH keys directly on your FIDO2 security key with OpenSSH.
The whole point of this touch to sign is that it can't be hacked remotely
